mekayis.metin: (حَكَرَ) الْحَاءُ وَالْكَافُ وَالرَّاءُ أَصْلٌ وَاحِدٌ، وَهُوَ الْحَبْسُ. وَالْحُكْرَةُ: حَبْسُ الطَّعَامِ مَنْتَظِرًا لِغَلَائِهِ، وَهُوَ الْحُكْرُ، وَأَصْلُهُ فِي كَلَامِ الْعَرَبِ الْحَكَرُ، وَهُوَ الْمَاءُ الْمُجْتَمِعُ، كَأَنَّهُ احْتُكِرَ لِقِلَّتِهِ.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: اِحْتِكَار • (iḥtikār) m (plural اِحْتِكَارَات (iḥtikārāt))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Verbal noun of اِحْتَكَرَ (iḥtakara).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: اِحْتَكَرَ • (iḥtakara) VIII (non-past يَحْتَكِرُ (yaḥtakiru), verbal noun اِحْتِكَار (iḥtikār))
مُحْتَكِر • (muḥtakir) m (plural مُحْتَكِرُون (muḥtakirūn))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Derived from the active participle of اِحْتَكَرَ (iḥtakara).

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: حَاكُورَة • (ḥākūra) f (plural حَوَاكِير (ḥawākīr))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t:
Absent from Classical dictionaries. The nomenclature of the Sultanate of Darfur's hakura system backdates the term's advent in Standard Arabic to the 18th century at latest, although the actual Darfur charters allegedly only rarely used حَاكُورَة (ḥākūra), preferring إقْطَاع (ʔiqṭāʕ); indeed, the 18th-century Taj al-Arus, whose Cairene author ought to have at the least been familiar with Sudan, only identifies حَاكُورَة (ḥākūra) as a Levantine or Syrian vernacularism. Its transmission into Cypriot Arabic as xakúra moreover suggests it is a relatively old one. Therefore, presumably originally innovated in older North Levantine Arabic and only in modern times incorporated into the standard language.
Compare حِكْر (ḥikr, “plot of land held in retention; monopoly”) and the verb حَكَرَ (ḥakara, “to hoard, to retain, to fence in”).
g: a small, fenced, or enclosed plot of cultivated land or orchard directly adjacent to or surrounding a house

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: حَكَرَ • (ḥakara) I (non-past يَحْكَرُ (yaḥkaru), verbal noun حَكْر (ḥakr))
g: to wrong (someone), to act wrongfully or injuriously (towards someone)
to act (towards someone) with bad fellowship, with difficulty or hardness
to bring (upon someone) distress or trouble

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: حَكَرَ • (ḥakara) I (non-past يَحْكِرُ (yaḥkiru), verbal noun حَكَر (ḥakar))
g: to be obstinate or persistent in contention
to keep a thing to himself, not allowing anyone to share with him in it

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: حِكْر • (ḥikr) m (plural أحْكَار)
g: what is enclosed (of lands and or houses) and debarred from others, so that they may not build upon it nor otherwise make use of it.

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: حَكَر • (ḥakar) m
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: verbal noun of حَكِرَ (ḥakira) (form I)
g: what is withheld (of wheat, and the like of what is eaten) in expectation of its becoming dear

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: حَكِر • (ḥakir)
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: Derived from the active participle of حَكَرَ (ḥakara).
g: one who withholds a thing and keeps it to himself
one who withholds or collects and withholds wheat, and the like, of what is eaten
one who ceases not to withhold his merchandise when the market is full of people and goods for sale, that is may be sold for much.
